text:
The story around Jakob Chychrun this month isn't his scoring. On Nov. 10 his hit on Ottawa's Nick Cousins, a former Coyotes teammate, knocked Cousins unconscious and out 7 to 10 days. The on-ice officials reviewed it and took back the major, and there was no suspension, but the reaction has dragged on for a week, Cousins unfollowing him included.

On the ice, Chychrun is playing a lot (24:16 a night) and getting little back for it. He has two goals on 60 shots, a 3.3% shooting rate against 8% we'd expect, and the Capitals have scored 4.4 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him out there. Thirteen points in 19 games is fine for a defenseman; our range says more is coming.

Evolving-Hockey had him as one of the league's better play-drivers last season (2.3 wins, 23rd among defensemen, with his team creating more with him on), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the slot more than most defensemen. The process is there. Washington has lost four straight, and he has no points in the last three.
